items.title: Final Fantasy XIV Players Mourn The Primals Bassist With In-Game Funerals and Gatherings
items.description: Final Fantasy XIV players are paying tribute to the bassist of the game’s official band, mourning him and celebrating his legacy with virtual, in-game funerals across servers worldwide.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Final Fantasy XIV players are paying tribute to the bassist of the game’s official band, mourning him and celebrating his legacy with virtual, in-game funerals across servers worldwide.

Eikichi Iwai was the bass guitarist for The Primals, a band formed specifically to make some of the music in Square Enix’s extremely popular MMORPG. While they aren’t the only ones responsible for some of the game’s iconic tunes, they’re certainly some of the most notable, and they’ve become a firm fixture in the Final Fantasy fanbase over the years.

Iwai’s death was officially announced on November 11, 2026 by his own rock band, Chirinuruwowa, and the Final Fantasy XIV development team, the latter of which penned a public letter to fans informing them of the news.

“As announced earlier today, we are deeply saddened to share the news of the sudden passing of bassist Eikichi Iwai,” the statement reads. “Having witnessed his truly unforgettable performance on stage at the recent FINAL FANTASY XIV Fan Festival in Japan, the sudden news of his passing has come as a profound shock. The members of THE PRIMALS and the entire FFXIV Development and Operations teams are overcome with deep sorrow.

“As we reflect on all that Eikichi-san has left behind, our thoughts are with him, and we offer our heartfelt condolences.”

Chirinuruwowa published a similar statement on social media. “We regret to inform you that our bassist, Iwaieikichi, has passed away suddenly,” the group wrote. “The sudden news of his passing has left all of us in the band and on the staff struggling to come to terms with it, and we are deeply saddened.” The band also informed fans that all upcoming performances in their Endless Loop 2026 -Public- tour have been cancelled.

Iwai's death sent shockwaves throughout the FFXIV playerbase. In acknowledgement of his legacy as a performer and paying tribute to his contributions to the game, these players gathered together within their respective servers to hold virtual funerals in some of the MMORPG’s fantastical locales.

For example, players on the European server Omega formed a circle around Limsa Lominsa’s Aetheryte Plaza, lighting campfires in remembrance of the bassist. And in the Sephirot, Materia DC server, players hung out for more than seven hours at Ultima Thule, calmly sitting in its field of flowers.

Fans, content creators, and fellow members of the games industry have shared their own fond memories of the game and the impact Iwai's music had on their lives.

@FF_XIV_EN A small memorial for Eikichi Iwai on Omega (Chaos). Thank you for everything, Iwai-san. Your final performance at Tokyo Fan Fest was incredible Chaos DC・オメガでイワイエイキチさんを偲ぶ小さな集まりを開きます。 イワイさん、ありがとう。東京ファンフェスでの最後の演奏最高でした https://t.co/2204TnVxIU

— Lorenzo (@_kefka_) November 11, 2026

Somehow some people are still here 7 hours later (I've just been doing other stuff)

I'll just leave my character here overnight as I'm going to sleep if anyone wants to continue the memorial feel free to come here at Ultima Thule, Sephirot, Materia DC

#THEPRIMALS #ffxiv https://t.co/l0YB7Ny45Q

— Veridis (@VeridisArpegius) November 11, 2026

イワイエイキチさん

いつも素晴らしいエネルギッシュなLIVEをありがとうございました

イフリート鯖のイフリートの祭壇 (X35.2 Y19.8)の追悼の場からお悔やみ申し上げます

#FF14

#THEPRIMALS https://t.co/Mi2oJtMiS5

— おーびー (@IMPAWD) November 11, 2026

“This one truly hurts… Words just can't describe the shock and grief I'm feeling right now,” YouTuber and game composer Alex Moukala wrote. “FFXIV fans lost an absolute icon. Many bass players around the world lost a hero. And those who knew Eikichi-san personally lost an incredibly kind friend. Rest in peace, Eikichi-san.”

“Eikichi-san was an absolute legend. This is so sudden and devastating. My sincere condolences to his family and friends. May he rest in peace,” another fan said.

Iwai was 57 years old at the time of his death. He joined The Primals in 2014 and has been performing with the band ever since. The group held a concert at a Final Fantasy XIV Fan Festival in Tokyo, Japan on November 1, and further performances were planned for Chirinuruwowa — concerts that have since been canceled in the wake of this tragic news.

items.title: CD Projekt Red Used AI to Alter Geralt's Voice Due to Polish Actor's Health Issues
items.description: The Witcher 3 is getting a new expansion more than 11 years after it first released, and due to a health issue experienced by Geralt's Polish voice actor, CD Projekt Red will be using an AI tool to modify his voice.
items.author: Jacqueline Thomas
items.content:
The Witcher 3 is getting a new expansion more than 11 years after it first released, and due to a health issue experienced by Geralt's Polish voice actor, CD Projekt Red will be using an AI tool to modify his voice.

Jacek Rozenek, who voiced Geralt in The Witcher 3's Polish dub, will be returning to voice Geralt in Songs of the Past. Rozenek notably suffered a stroke back in 2019 that affected his voice. Thanks to modern technology, CD Projekt Red is able to use an AI voice modulator, Respeecher, to alter the actor's voice to match his 2014 lines, as noted by Game File.

According to the post, Rozenek's stroke left him unable to even speak for a while, and he only gained his voice back after a ton of rigorous training. He was able to return for a couple of quests in the Next-Gen update that came out back in 2022, but told Game File that he "was so exhausted after this recording." Still, CD Projekt Red wanted him to return for the new expansion, so it had to think outside the box.

The main problem was that, after everything Rozenek went through, his voice was noticably different than it was in 2014 when he recorded the bulk of Geralt's lines for the original game. Rozenek's voice is now much lower pitched than it used to be, which would make any new lines sound odd when played next to the older ones that are supposed to take place in the same time period. Hence, the need for Respeecher.

Respeecher's model was trained on all of Rozenek's lines from the original game, but it sounds like this was doing a lot more than just running his voice through a quick filter. When asked about the process, Respeecher synthetic speech artist Dmytro Vasylets told Game File that "getting there took dozens of hours, training models, going through the details with the CDPR team, and dealing with AI artifacts that never fully disappear."

CDPR got Rozenek's blessing to use the tool, who told Game File, "I have great trust… for the creators of this game," and that, "when it comes to the dynamics of the voice, when it comes to the acting aspects, I feel very good, really very good."

Still, CDPR is aware of the optics of using AI anywhere near a voice actor, and it stressed to Game File that this was a special case. CD Projekt Red localization producer Mikołaj Szwed told the publication that the company wouldn't be using any AI tools to alter someone's voice without the express permission of that voice actor.

Even for The Witcher 4, which Rozenek is expected to return for, the tool won't be needed, due to Geralt being older and more grizzled, so a deeper voice won't be so jarring.

But while this seems like a good use of AI, the technology is still extremely controversial in gaming. Last year, the Indie Game Awards stripped the Game of the Year award from Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 after AI-generated placeholder textures were found in the game. Players have also found AI-generated art in Crimson Desert, though it's since been patched out.

items.title: New GTA 6 Surprise Gameplay Seemingly Released in Yet Another Viral Marketing Stunt
items.description: Rockstar Games appears to have released new footage from GTA 6, which also recreates the studio's real-life viral marketing in-game.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Rockstar Games appears to have released new footage from GTA 6, which also recreates the studio's real-life viral marketing in-game.

A new Instagram post from the account "Only in Dade" began to raise eyebrows earlier today, as it appeared to contain legitimate footage of GTA 6. The footage shows someone driving down Ocean Drive, recording a bunch of flashy cars lined up while people wander past. A second person on the sidewalk recorded the exact same video from a different perspective. Some fans think that the two people recording are Jason and Lucia, respectively, though the footage isn't clear enough to be able to confidently make that determination.

Many were wondering if this was AI footage or a render until Rockstar Games reposted it on its Instagram story and liked the video, indicating this is likely real in-game footage. The studio is very careful and calculated with what it chooses to post and interact with, so it isn't going around liking random AI-generated clips of its upcoming game.

However, what's even more interesting is that this footage directly recreates a real-life video from last month. Rockstar teamed up with West Coast Customs to bring cars from GTA 6 to real life and spent October parading them around the city of Miami. As a result, there were tons of videos and social media posts about these vehicles, and one has now seemingly been recreated in GTA 6. You can see the same people, including a person on a motorized scooter and a man taking pictures in front of one of the cars, all replicated in the GTA 6 footage above.

It's clear that Rockstar's marketing strategy has gotten extremely creative, and it's a bit of a flex to produce something that has many wondering if the visuals are too good to be true. Rockstar also pulled off a similar stunt a couple of weeks ago when it debuted a tiny bit of new gameplay during an episode of South Park. The footage wasn't advertised ahead of time, so people also thought that it might be AI-generated gameplay until Rockstar's name was discovered in the credits.

The hype for GTA 6 is currently at its peak, releasing in just one week. The launch represents the end of a 13-year journey for many fans, as Rockstar hasn't made a new GTA game since 2013. There was, of course, Red Dead Redemption 2 in 2018, which certainly helped tide some fans over... but that was still nearly a decade ago at this point.

Pre-loading has officially begun so fans can prepare for their trip to Vice City next week. Rockstar has also released new trailers, screenshots, and other marketing beats, which have created a flury of speculation over what may or may not be in the game. Thankfully, we won't have to wait much longer to find out.

items.title: Nintendo Takes Down Switch Emulators and Mod Chip Firmware in Massive GitHub DMCA Sweep
items.description: Nintendo has sent four DMCA takedown notices to GitHub targeting two Nintendo Switch emulators, Yuzu and Citron Neo, along with mod chip firmware.
items.author: Jacqueline Thomas
items.content:
Nintendo has sent four DMCA takedown notices to GitHub targeting two Nintendo Switch emulators, Yuzu and Citron Neo, along with mod chip firmware.

This isn't the first time Nintendo has sent takedown notices to GitHub, and it's not even the first time it's tried to take down Yuzu, but the focus this time around seems to be on firmware for mod chips. This particular firmware had 144 repositories, all of which have been removed by GitHub and replaced by a DMCA takedown notice. Mod chips like Picofly can be soldered onto the Nintendo Switch's mainboard, and can be flashed with this firmware to circumvent Nintendo's copy protection.

GitHub has posted Nintendo's November 6 DMCA notice, which says, "The Nintendo Switch console and video games contain technological protection measures ('TPMs') that permit the Nintendo Switch console to interact only with legitimate Nintendo video game files. This process protects Nintendo’s copyright-protected video games, (...) by preventing users from playing pirated copies of Nintendo’s video games on the Nintendo Switch console and by preventing users from unlawfully copying and playing Nintendo’s video games on unauthorized devices."

However, while this takedown has effectively wiped out a ton of repositories with mod chip firmware, it seems like it's still being hosted elsewhere on the site, according to TorrentFreak. It's possible, though, that Nintendo isn't finished yet; back in 2024, Nintendo effectively took down 8,500 copies of Yuzu by issuing a takedown that targeted 12 different mirrors of the emulator.

This particular takedown also comes a few days after emulators were able to run the remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on PC, so this could be a sign that Nintendo is winding up its lawyers to crack down on emulation once again.

If anything, emulation is a completely different beast in 2026 than it was even in 2024, thanks to the rise of AI. There's already been a wave of AI-made mashup mods that took over Twitter for a couple of weeks, and led Anthropic to coding in a lock to prevent Claude from outright copying games. Game developers have started cracking down on AI ports of games, too. Just last month Rockstar had to take down a browser version of GTA 5, and Bethesda took down an AI-generated Fallout New York game.

items.title: Street Fighter Just Barely Fails to Fight Off Original Street Fighter at the Box Office as New Movie Leaves 1,700 Theaters
items.description: The 2026 Street Fighter film has just barely fallen short of dethroning the original 1994 movie, which still holds its record as the highest-grossing Street Fighter adaptation put to screens.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
The 2026 Street Fighter film has just barely fallen short of dethroning the original 1994 movie, which still holds its record as the highest-grossing Street Fighter adaptation put to screens.

Legendary’s Street Fighter movie hurricane-kicked its way into theaters on October 16, 2026. Almost a month later, it hasn't managed to surpass its predecessor, earning a tentative $99.2 million worldwide as of November 10. Estimates show that the fighting game flick earned $57.4 million domestically in North America and $41.7 million internationally. It's now approaching the end of its theatrical run, having left 1,700 theaters as of mid-November.

The so-bad-it’s-good Street Fighter movie from 1994, starring Raul Julia and Jean-Claude Van Damme, garnered just a smidge over this amount; Estimates show that it earned approximately $99,431,786 at the global box office, divided into $33,423,521 domestically and $66,008,265 internationally.

The 2026 Street Fighter flick, starring Andrew Koji, Callina Liang, and Noah Centineo — as well as a host of wrestling royalty and music artists — was made on a reported budget of $80 million, not including marketing. This means that it has profited about $20 million near the end of its theatrical run, but there’s still time for a streaming release to bump those numbers up even more. A 4K Steelbook release has also been confirmed, with two variant covers featuring either heroes or villains.

The movie enjoyed a successful opening weekend, topping the box office at $51.1 million. However, it experienced a major dropoff in the following weeks, though it seems to have enjoyed a steady influx of theater viewers despite this fact.

That’s optimistic news for fans who are hoping for a sequel; speaking on social media, Zangief actor Olivier Richters revealed that the movie’s entire cast signed on for a trilogy, explaining that some characters didn’t receive the amount of screentime some viewers were expecting, as plans had already been laid to flesh them out further in following films.

The movie did end on a cliffhanger, setting itself up for a sequel to finally introduce a long-awaited character who was notably absent from the first flick. Speaking with the cast and director Kitao Sakurai, it’s clear that all those involved want to make another movie in the Street Fighter universe — but this hinges on how much money the first movie ends up making.

Sakurai revealed that a sequel is already being written, so it’s clear that plans are laid for more movies. For now, we’ll just have to wait and see what the future holds for Capcom’s fighting game franchise on the silver screen.

In the meantime, you can check out our interviews with the Street Fighter cast, who told us that they would love to film a crossover flick with the Mortal Kombat crew, or check out our chat with Olivier Richters, who admitted that he wants to become the ‘Ultimate Zangief’ and compete in Street Fighter tournaments using the character — something he actually did over the weekend at a tournament in the Netherlands.

items.title: Roblox Horror Hit Dandy's World Is Finally Leaving Alpha With a Massive 1.0 Update, New Game Mode, and More
items.author: Rachel Weber
items.content:
Roblox mascot horror hit Dandy's World is finally leaving Alpha, with developer BlushCrunch Studio announcing that its massive 1.0 update will arrive on November 20, 2026, bringing a brand-new game mode, more than 10 new floors, and a hefty lump of lore for fans.

For the uninitiated, Dandy's World is a co-op survival horror game in which players take control of adorable characters known as Toons and work together to survive increasingly dangerous floors of the abandoned Gardenview Center. Naturally, there's a catch: the building is crawling with monstrous creatures called Twisteds, and surviving means completing objectives while avoiding a particularly unpleasant fate.

Since launching in Alpha more than two years ago, Dandy's World has become one of Roblox's breakout horror hits, racking up over 7 billion lifetime plays and building an enormous community around its cast of more than 40 playable Toons. Now, BlushCrunch Studio is giving the game a mega update.

The headline addition in the 1.0 update is Dandy's World's first-ever new game mode, offering a more challenging alternative to the familiar survival experience. This includes an entirely new path through Gardenview Center, with more than 10 additional floors taking players into the building's deepest and darkest areas.

There are also new gameplay systems to contend with, including a card system and a new coordinator NPC whose decision-making algorithm reacts and adapts to how players approach each run. Exactly how these systems will work remains to be seen, but they should introduce some interesting new wrinkles to the game's cooperative survival formula.

"Even though this 1.0 update brings us out of Alpha, this is just the beginning for Dandy's World. We have so much more planned for next year, on Roblox and beyond," said Joe Jurbala, president of BlushCrunch Studio.

For fans who are more interested in uncovering the mysteries of Gardenview than simply surviving them, the update also includes over 10,000 words of new lore and dialogue. It'll explore the origins of the Gardenview Center and the events leading up to the mysterious Malfunction Incident, potentially answering some of the questions that have kept the game's fans theorizing like conspiracy theorists.

And BlushCrunch isn't stopping at the game itself. On November 19, the day before the update launches, the studio will release the full theme song for the fictional Dandy's World animated series across music streaming platforms. Fans are also getting a fully animated music video introducing a brand-new character, alongside the return of Dandy's World's annual month-long Christmas event.

items.title: GTA 6 Fans Think a Beloved Legacy Character from a Previous Game Is Hiding in the Latest Trailer
items.description: The most recent GTA 6 trailer has many people wondering if an iconic character from a previous game in the franchise is making a return.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
The most recent GTA 6 trailer has many people wondering if an iconic character from a previous game in the franchise is making a return.

In the latest GTA 6 trailer, released yesterday to announce pre-loads, a character in a blue tank top and bulky black glasses is seen saying, "Oh, it is so on now." This is seemingly the first time we've seen this mystery character in GTA 6, and there may be a reason for that. Some fans believe this is an older and slightly chubbier Tony Prince (AKA Gay Tony). The character made his debut in GTA 4 and appeared in both DLCs, but was the focus of The Ballad of Gay Tony expansion. In that story, players filled the shoes of Luis, Tony's right-hand man. Tony Prince was a prominent nightclub owner in Liberty City, but he has since bounced around.

Why does this guy actually kinda look and sound like Tony? I’m losing my mind, similar glasses, beard and very similar voice.

There’s no way he let himself go and moved to the keys right? https://t.co/NH1Ltr7I93

— TGG (@TGGonYT) November 11, 2026

Tony moved to Los Santos years later and returned in a GTA Online update, giving missions to the player as part of the game's nightclub operations. Now, some fans believe he may have moved to Vice City/Leonida, though he may have fallen on hard times. He looks more out of shape, he's missing his high-end sense of style, minus the glasses, and he doesn't appear to be living it up in a highrise apartment or anything like that.

The character has the same style of beard, glasses, and has a similar voice to Tony, but it's hard to say if it really is him. It could be someone who somewhat resembles him, but the speculation is driving some fans mad. GTA 6 will lean pretty heavily on Vice City's nightlife, with clubbing being prominently featured in the trailers released by Rockstar (including the pre-load ad). One of the in-game clubs, known as Jack of Hearts, is also expected to be a haven for celebrities and real-life musicans. Travis Scott namedropped it in his song, RHYNO, which will be featured in the game, and a screenshot revealed Kodak Black will hang out there as an NPC.

Naturally, it would make tons of sense for GTA's nightclub king to be part of the festivities in Vice City. We'll ultimately just have to wait and see, but thankfully, we are only days away from finding out. We have just a week left until GTA 6 launches, and it looks like it's going to make a big splash. The game is currently the most pre-ordered game in the history of the Xbox and PlayStation digital stores, suggesting all kinds of sales records will be broken next weekend.

items.title: Ocarina of Time Remake Players Stunned After Learning a Family Guy Meme Works to Summon Epona
items.description: As it turns out, saying, “Petah, the horse is here,” in the voice of Lois Griffin while the Ocarina of Time remake is in microphone mode somehow gets recognized as Epona’s Song, allowing you to successfully call your pony.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
The Ocarina of Time Remake is taking over social media as players share their experiences traversing through the well-worn paths of Hyrule three decades after the first game was released — but it’s got a few new features that are sending fans into a tizzy.

For one, the new Ocarina remake has an option that lets players use the Nintendo Switch 2’s built-in microphone to hum, whistle, sing, or play an actual instrument to produce the tunes that Link plays on his Ocarina, rather than pushing corresponding buttons on the console’s controller. This feature isn’t exactly fine-tuned, as players have uploaded oodles of videos showing themselves singing completely different songs that somehow seem to work.

One of these humorous videos has gone viral on social media, leaving players totally shocked that it actually gets the intended result. On Twitter/X, a user named ‘Rubix’ discovered that a well-known meme from Family Guy is close enough to Epona’s Song that it actually summons Link’s trusty steed.

As it turns out, saying, “Petah, the horse is here,” in the voice of Lois Griffin while the game is in microphone mode gets recognized as Epona’s Song, allowing you to successfully call your pony. It’s worth noting that the console matches a specific song to the tune of whatever you’re singing or humming (or, in this case, saying in a nasally Long Island accent), provided it’s a close enough match — and apparently, this famous line was a dead ringer for Epona’s Song.

It’s not just a one-off, either; one half of the content creator duo 'BungleDungle' also tried this trick and was left totally stunned after it worked for him, too.

For those out of the loop, this meme comes from Season 7, Episode 8 of Family Guy, which aired in 2009. In the episode, Peter buys a brain-damaged racehorse at an auction. In the specific scene being referenced, the horse peeks its head into the dining room as the Griffin family is having dinner, prompting Lois to say, “Petah, the horse is here.”

IT ACTUALLY DID https://t.co/ejF1c6rtys

— BungleDungle_YT - TheOnePhun211🇨🇦🇮🇹🇵🇭 (@BungleDungle_YT) November 11, 2026

It’s a fairly innocuous line that has become an in-joke for Family Guy fans over the years, eventually evolving into a meme that continues to live on nearly 20 years later.

Other hilarious clips from players saying wild things into their Nintendo Switch 2’s microphones have also gone viral, like this video from streamer Lythero saying “Mark Zuckerberg” into the mic in a vague approximation of the Song of Passing that actually got recognized as the short ditty, turning night to day.

So you can sing songs to your controller and it's the best streamer gag

https://t.co/qIU0Oai1C0 https://t.co/bPxqzecs9U

— Lythero 🎮 (@Lythero) November 9, 2026

The Ocarina of Time remake has been a standout success for Nintendo, selling over five million copies in just four days. It’s also garnered rave reviews from both fans and critics alike, with IGN’s Logan Plant scoring the game a glowing 9 out of 10, praising it for “skillfully melding the world and dungeon design of classic Zeldas with the movement and presentation of its more recent games, creating both a beautiful retelling of a legend and a rich adventure that stands on its own.”

items.title: MSI Is Raising Graphics Cards Prices Again in China, According to Leak
items.description: Ever since the RAM crisis kicked off in earnest in November 2025, pretty much every component in a gaming PC has grown more expensive. And now, less than a month after the RTX 5080 hit $2,000 here in the US, it's reportedly going to get even more expensive in China.
items.author: Jacqueline Thomas
items.content:
Ever since the RAM crisis kicked off in earnest in November 2025, pretty much every component in a gaming PC has grown more expensive. Now, less than a month after the RTX 5080 hit $2,000 here in the U.S., it's reportedly going to get even more expensive in China.

According to a post on ChannelGate, a Chinese tech insider board on WeChat, and spotted by Nvidia leaker Harukaze5719 on Twitter, MSI has increased GPU prices in China across the board, but the biggest increase is hitting the RTX 5080. Nvidia's penultimate GPU is going going up from 1,300 to 8,000 Yuan, or $194 to $1,199. However, lower-specced GPUs will have much less of a price increase, with the RTX 5060 only going up between 200 to 500 Yuan, or $30 to $75.

When Nvidia unveiled its Blackwell lineup of graphics cards, the RTX 5080 was already expensive, starting at $999, even though it was hard to find at that price for a while. But right when prices started to normalize, the RAM crisis happened, and prices have been steadily going up since February.

Even according to the leaks, these price increases are only going to hit in China, but it's likely that they'll eventually filter through to the U.S. At the time of writing, the RTX 5080 starts at around $2,199 on Newegg, and if these price increases came to the U.S., that'd go up to at least $2,400, and would likely be even higher.

These Chinese price increases are coming a couple of weeks after Nvidia removed the RTX 5080 from its own storefront, due to hardware shortages. Nvidia has told me that it's going to continue making the RTX 5080 and that it'll reappear on the Nvidia marketplace when supply has stabilized, but with these kinds of price increases, it's anyone's guess on when that'll happen.

It's clear that the RAM crisis is going to worsen a bit in 2027. In its latest earnings call, Samsung, which makes a huge portion of the world's RAM supply, has said that it expects supply to tighten in the next year. Meanwhile, multiple RAM manufacturers have sold through their entire manufacturing capacity through the next year, leaving very little for consumers. And even though AI companies are getting a lion's share of the world's memory supply, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said in an interview last month that it's "quite terrible" that people have RAM in their own PCs.

items.title: How About a GTA Set Outside the United States? 'Never Say Never,' Rockstar Boss Teases, but Don't Hold Your Breath
items.description: Rockstar isn't ruling out a GTA set outside the United States, but don't hold your breath: the studio says there are plenty more stories to tell in America.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Rockstar isn't ruling out a GTA set outside the United States, but don't hold your breath: the studio says there are plenty more stories to tell in America.

In an interview with The Guardian, Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson was asked whether or not the developer would ever make a GTA game set outside of America. His response was simple: "Never say never." However, Nelson continued his response by stating, "There’s still so much to do in America."

The GTA series has largely rotated between three locations for the last 25 years: Liberty City (New York), Vice City (Miami), and San Andreas (California). We got a brief glimpse at the Midwest of GTA in GTA 5, when the game's story opened in a snowy state called North Yankton. But that's about as much as we've gotten outside of the coastal cities that GTA rotates through. It's unclear what else Rockstar wants to do with GTA, specifically the American setting.

GTA has flirted with going overseas before, as Rockstar came close to making one set in Japan in the early to mid-2000s. The first GTA also had an expansion set in London, and GTA 5 seemingly had scrapped DLC that would've at least partially taken place in Paris. Ex-GTA writer and creative director Dan Houser also stated last year that he doesn't think GTA would work as well outside of America.

"I think for a full GTA game, we always decided there was so much Americana inherent in the IP, it would be really hard to make it work in London or anywhere else," said Houser. "You know, you needed guns, you needed these larger-than-life characters. It just felt like the game was so much about America, possibly from an outsider's perspective. But that was so much about what the thing was that it wouldn't really have worked in the same way elsewhere.”

Maybe one day it will happen, but it does seem like Rockstar's interests with GTA are rooted in American culture.

GTA 6 will, of course, take us back to Vice City next week when it launches on November 19. It is expected to have one of the biggest launches in history, with it already being the most preordered game in the history of Xbox and PlayStation's digital stores. Players are able to preload the game right now, and they absolutely should, as the game is a whopping 210 GBs.

items.title: WoW Forever's First Big Secret Has Been Discovered by Players
items.description: If there's one thing that's true about any version of World of Warcraft it's that Blizzard loves hiding convoluted quest chains behind mundane objects, the first of which has been found in WoW Forever.
items.author: Jacqueline Thomas
items.content:
If there's one thing that's true about any version of World of Warcraft, it's that Blizzard loves hiding convoluted quest chains behind mundane objects, the first of which has been found in WoW Forever.

If you've started a Skyborne character in Forever, you've probably completed a quest that rewarded you with an 'Ancient Heirloom' ring with no stats, and wondered why it even exists. Well, it turns out that it kicks off a whole hidden quest chain if you know where to look.

This secret was discovered by the WoW Secret Finding and Collections Discord, and it involves getting that ring, finding a sword hilt that only shows up when you're using a specific torch, then finding a blade with a random location and then finding and cleansing a 'Befouled Water Globe.' The community has put together a guide on Wowhead of the known steps so far, but there's a catch – it doesn't seem like anyone has actually finished the little scavenger hunt yet.

As of this morning, folks in the WoW Secret Finding Discord are still actively trying to see what gets unlocked at the end of this convoluted chain, but for now, the community is calling it the "Dawn Waker Secret" and seems to believe it revolves around a couple of swords: Eluvi'ana and Eluvi'tor.

As part of the process, you'll end up with a sword that you need to cleanse, and to do that, you'll need to clear the Capital Gardens section of Dire Maul and talk to Prince Tortheldrin, whose dialog hints that "such knowledge is reserved by those honored in my royal court." And, in classic WoW fashion, this probably means a lengthy rep grind is needed.

According to admin Miko in the WoW Secret Finding Discord, "Our most recent discoveries hint us that the rewards for this chain will involve the swords of Eluvi'ana and Eluvi'tor. The most recent step points us to a rep grind with the Shendralar Faction, as Prince Tortheldrin in Dire Maul tells us that only those Honored with his court are worthy enough to obtain the knowledge about these blades."

Depending on how long it takes players to actually get Honored with the Shendralar faction, it might be a while before the final reward is actually revealed. But there are hundreds of players in this Discord channel working on the secret, so it's only a matter of time.

We're still in the early days of WoW Forever, after all, and it's been a massively successful launch. And as more players start to get to max level, more secrets are sure to pop up in the world. After all, while World of Warcraft takes a lot of queues from Classic WoW, the developers have added a ton of content, so who knows how many secrets have been buried in the corners of Azeroth?

items.description: Bethesda has issued an official response to fans expecting a major announcement for The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel at some point today.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Bethesda has issued an official response to fans expecting a major announcement for The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel at some point today.

In a post from the company's official account on reddit, Bethesda said it had seen the growing speculation among its fans that today, November 11, would bring more details on Sentinel, hot on the heels of the game's subtitle and logo reveal just last week.

Alas, today will not be when we find out more about the game, Bethesda has now said — pouring cold water on hopes that we would see more of the Hammerfell-set role-player anytime soon.

Despite being announced eight years ago, Sentinel is reportedly still two years away from launch — at least. We don't even know which platforms it will launch on (could it be an Xbox Helix launch title?) or whether it will be an Xbox console exclusive. Of course, that hasn't stopped Bethesda already beginning to sell Sentinel merch.

"Hey everyone, wanted to pop in to say that we aren't going to have any big announcements tomorrow," Bethesda wrote overnight (tomorrow meaning today, November 11). "We're excited you're excited but we will not be sharing anything new on Sentinel for some time."

Response to that statement is unsurprisingly a little mixed, with some fans commenting that they appreciate the clarity from Bethesda, while others joking that it will be another eight years before we see anything more of the game.

Of course, November 11 is an important date in the minds of The Elder Scrolls fans. It is the original release date for The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim, all the way back in 2011 (memorably, on 11/11/11). 15 years on, you can see why some had hoped Bethesda might have more to say today — but alas that is not set to be the case.

For those wanting to read more Sentinel today, however, IGN has you covered. We've got a deep dive on what Sentinel actually means based on The Elder Scrolls lore, and why Sentinel's in-universe quote teaser is sparking particular timeline speculation. We also have a roundup of former Bethesda design director Bruce Nesmith's wishes for Sentinel, whenever the long-awaited game does finally arrive.

items.title: Blizzard Changes World of Warcraft Forever Gold Rewards for High Level Quests, and Players Are Celebrating
items.description: For the longest time in World of Warcraft, when you finished a quest at max level, the experience you would earn would get converted to gold. But in WoW Forever, Blizzard killed off that conversion, and has now added a fix.
items.author: Jacqueline Thomas
items.content:
For the longest time in World of Warcraft, when you finished a quest at max level, the experience you would earn would get converted to gold. But in WoW Forever, Blizzard killed off that conversion, and has now added a fix.

The experience-to-gold conversion for quests completed at high level has been a part of WoW for nearly 20 years, to the point where a lot of players rely on it to build up some cash when they hit max level, especially in the Classic versions of the game. But, when WoW Forever launched last week, that conversion was missing, and now that players are starting to hit level 60, they're starting to feel that loss of gold.

Thankfully, Blizzard community manager Kaivax has posted on the WoW forum to say a hotfix will go live "in the next 24 hours or so" to help high level players earn a little bit of gold. Rather than converting experience to gold, Blizzard will buff the gold rewarded for high level quests, regardless of what level you are.

According to Kaivax: "We’re preparing a hotfix that will add additional gold rewards to most quests with a quest level of level 48 or higher, including adding gold to quests above level 48 that never previously rewarded gold at all. The idea here is that you should feel good about doing quests at the appropriate level to progress your character, and you should feel adequately rewarded with gold for doing so."

But why change that experience-gold conversion in the first place? Well, according to Kaivax, that conversion "created an incentive for players to hold a full quest log worth of completed quests to hand in after hitting level 60 for maximum gold returns. Under those conditions, the optimal way for players to level to 60 was to simply grind creatures for XP and not hand in quests at all, which is not a design we want to retain in WoW: Forever."

Kaivax's post was in a thread where players were complaining about not being able to earn gold from quests. The original post was from Faze, who said four days ago that "the change to not give additional gold in exchange for EXP at 60 needs to be reverted. Quests are basically useless at 60 if they don’t have a reward. This was one of the easy ways to make gold to afford spells and mounts. This is a horrible design and change. It feels good to complete quests and now this just feels BAD at 60. Change this back ASAP."

Before Kaivax posted, nearly 100 replies deep, there were a ton of players who were essentially saying that they'd stop playing the game over this. Player Glôwstick said, "This is a deal breaker for me, wont be playing any more until this is reverted," while Rackjaw commented, "WoW Forever devs seem to be obsessed with 'fixing' things that aren’t broken."

However, players seem to have changed their tune immediately after Kaivax's response. Danni said: "Nice change. Quests giving consistent gold whether you do them at 59 or 60 makes sense, and doesn’t punish people for handing them in 'too soon.'"

There are some players that are skeptical about the change. For instance, Jalesanda posted: "I will withhold putting the pitch forks away for now until we see how much gold this is, and how it compares. But it’s put down, for now."

This change really does highlight the philosophy that the WoW Forever team is taking with the new game mode, though. While there are players who probably want a 1:1 copy of Classic, Forever will make changes as long as they stay within the 'spirit' of the game. That's why, for instance, the devs held the line on group tagging, but had no problem adding some quests like the beloved 'Kyle's Gone Missing' or changing how dungeon experience is earned.

And as more players start to reach max level, the initial design of WoW Forever is going to be pushed to its limits, and we'll just have to see the extent of changes that Blizzard is going to be willing to make. Right now, WoW Forever is kind of like a blank canvass, and while I've been given some hints of where the game might go in the future, I can't wait to see the unique path Forever takes. And this experience to gold conversion change is really just the first of many changes I'm sure we're going to see.

items.title: Lanterns Writer Says 'Nothing's Cancelled. Calm Down' Amid Concern for Season 2 Following Shock DC Shakeup
items.description: Lanterns writer addresses concern over Season 2 amid DC shakeup.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Is Lanterns Season 2 happening or not? It’s unclear, following the shock exit of DC Studios co-CEOs James Gunn and Peter Safran. Yesterday, Variety reported that Lanterns "didn't get renewed for a second season," then updated the wording of its article to say the show "has yet to be renewed for a second season."

With Skydance and new DC boss Jeremy Latcham now in charge of all intellectual property under Warner Bros.’s banner, the future of the DCU is up in the air. Gunn’s own Man of Tomorrow and Matt Reeves’ The Batman Part II (the latter of which is not part of the DCU canon) still have theatrical release dates, but beyond that, what’s the plan? We don’t know.

Lanterns, which stars Kyle Chandler as Hal Jordan and Aaron Pierre as John Stewart, was well-received, and reports indicated a team had been assembled to write and produce Season 2, should it be greenlit. Here’s what Variety had to say about Lanterns, specifically:

“Lanterns, their first live-action TV show, had strong viewership and averaged 19 million viewers globally per episode going into the finale. Yet an insider at the company suggests the crime drama isn’t quite capturing the zeitgeist, pointing out the show has yet to be renewed for a second season.”

That doesn’t sound good for Lanterns Season 2, although we know Pierre’s John Stewart is set to star in next summer’s Man of Tomorrow. Countering the doom and gloom around Lanterns, however, is Chris Cantwell, co-creator of Halt and Catch Fire. He was drafted in to work on Lanterns Season 2 as a writer, producer, and showrunner, were it to actually happen, and he’s been vocal about the reports about the series fate on social media.

“Dear Internet,” he began. “I haven’t heard a f***ing thing. People sometimes wonder what future seasons of Halt and Catch Fire would’ve been. They would’ve arrived at social media and AI and the characters would’ve killed themselves.

“Nothing’s cancelled. Calm down.”

That sounds definitive, but as mentioned, neither James Gunn nor Jeremy Latcham have confirmed Season 2 is actually happening. Last month, then DC Studios co-CEO Peter Safran told IGN that a decision on Lanterns Season 2 would be made by the end of 2026.

Safran confirmed there was a writer's room hashing out ideas for the future of Lanterns, but it would all depend on whether or not they come up with a good enough story worthy of following up the first season. He noted that TV was an important part of DC's future, but that they were waiting to see if there was a story worth telling before giving the greenlight to Lanterns Season 2.

"The episodic world is always going to be a really important part of our overall slate, it's a great way to tell stories that need more real estate than a feature film can offer you, and it's a great way to introduce characters that we then bring into the feature world," said Safran. "And I think that Aaron Pierre and John Stewart are a perfect example of that. We introduced him in Lanterns, and audiences will see him next summer in Man of Tomorrow. So, it's really important to us in continuing to tell aspects of the story that we're not telling in the feature film world, so there's more to come.

"Listen, we'll see what happens with Lanterns Season 2. If, I think, the collective group of HBO and DC and Chris Mundy and the team all feel like we've got something that is a worthy successor to quite a beloved first season of television, then I wouldn't be surprised to see more."

But that was last month, and a lot has happened since then.

In the wake of the DC news, the Hollywood trades have reported that Skydance wasn't particularly impressed by the box office returns of Gunn's DCU, with even Superman apparently failing to do big enough numbers.

Predictably, fans of Zack Snyder’s DCEU have called for the Snyderverse to return, reinstating, for example, Henry Cavill as Superman and continuing where Snyder’s Justice League left off. There is no indication that Skydance will do so, but that hasn’t stopped fans comparing the box office returns of four years of the Snyderverse and four years of Gunn’s DCU.

We’ve got plenty more analysis of Gunn’s exit from DC Studios, including James Gunn and Peter Safran May Be Out, But Their DCU Needs to Continue, and The DCU and James Gunn's Batman Was Dead Before It Was Even Born.

items.title: Tekken Legend Katsuhiro Harada Says He Wishes 'Hardware Like the Xbox Series S Wouldn't Be Released'
items.description: Tekken development legend Katsuhiro Harada had some strong comments for Microsoft's lower-powered Xbox Series S console, dubbing it a "weaker child" with "awkwardly lower performance."
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Tekken development legend Katsuhiro Harada had some strong comments for Microsoft's lower-powered Xbox Series S console, dubbing it a "weaker child" with "awkwardly lower performance."

A number of video game developers have struggled with the Xbox Series S while following Microsoft's feature parity rules across Xbox Series consoles. Baldur's Gate 3 famously came to Xbox a few months late and required the help of Microsoft's engineers to get the game's split-screen co-op working on Series S. More recently, the developer of breakout shooter Wardogs admitted that the limitations of the Xbox Series S had stopped it from adding certain things to the game.

Indeed, one of the questions facing Microsoft ever since the release of the Xbox Series S back in 2020 is whether it would be willing to allow developers and publishers to release a game on Xbox Series X only, leaving Xbox Series S behind. As it stands, Xbox mandates that video games launch on both or none at all, and that there should be main feature parity between each version.

In a roundtable discussion held at the Console Game Developers Conference in Korea, Harada slammed the Series S and attempted to encourage Cyberpunk 2077 associate game director Paweł Sasko to join in the pile-on, too.

"There's something I really want to say while I have the floor," Harada began (thanks, Inven Global), "since a senior Xbox official is actually in attendance here today, I wish hardware like the Xbox Series S wouldn't be released (laughs)."

Throughout his years in charge of Tekken, Harada has become known as a colorful character happy to express his opinions freely. And, to be fair, it sounds like Harada made the comment knowing he was being rather cheeky. But the developer then continued to explain his position further — and have Sasko back him up, following reports that CD Projekt struggled with Cyberpunk 2077's Series S version.

"I want to ask director Paweł personally," Harada continued. "Honestly, weren't you upset inside because of Series S?"

"It constantly throws challenges at us and forces us to optimize our code very cleanly," Sasko responded, appearing to tiptoe around the subject.

"You just used a very polite and elegant way to say 'Xbox Series S sucks,' right?" Harada ploughed on. "Low memory is an issue, but the hardest part is that it's a device so similar to Series X while having awkwardly lower performance. When porting to Switch 2, developers can shift their mindset to 'Switch 2 is a distinct device for Nintendo fans!' But with Xbox, after delivering your absolute best output, it feels like having to do extra work for a slightly weaker child."

Gosh. Tell us what you really think, Harada!

"Furthermore," he continued further, "in markets like the U.S., there are more Series S users than Series X users, so we can't just cut corners. Yet after launch, Series S users direct their complaints at us developers rather than Microsoft, asking 'Why is texture resolution lower only on Series S?'"

While Harada's comments will likely not come as a shock to many developers who have been tasked with releasing games across the Xbox Series family this generation, it is rare to hear someone of Harada's prominence discussing the Series S' drawbacks out loud.

In response — and in a continued attempt to not say anything that would get him in trouble — Sasko acknowledged that such Series S drawbacks were real, but that the console also offered a lot of positives. Its more affordable price point meant that developers could get their games played by a wider audience, Sasko offered, while opimtization breakthroughs initially made for Series S had also benefited Cyberpunk 2077 across all platforms.

Acknowledging Sasko's more positive take, Harada concluded that he was now worried Microsoft would "feel reassured and release a successor like 'Helix S' for the next-gen Xbox as well (laughs)."

Will Xbox release a lower-powered Helix console? It's unclear. After earlier reports that suggested the new console was reportedly targeting a holiday 2027 launch, more recent estimates have pointed to a 2028 launch for the machine — at an eyewatering $1,200 - $1,800 price point. Maybe that will make Harada reconsider?

items.title: Colin Farrell Says 'There's a Conversation to Be Had' About The Penguin Season 2, Having Filmed Just 2 Scenes for The Batman Part II
items.description: Colin Farrell has confirmed he only appears in two scenes as the Penguin in The Batman Part II, but would love to play the character again in a potential Season 2 of the HBO show, insisting "there's a conversation to be had."
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Colin Farrell has confirmed he only appears in two scenes as the Penguin in The Batman Part II, but would love to play the character again in a potential Season 2 of the HBO show, insisting "there's a conversation to be had."

Farrell is set to don the prosthetics once again as the Penguin in The Batman Part II, now due out February 18, 2028, having played the character first in The Batman and again in the well-received The Penguin HBO Max show.

In an interview on UK show This Morning to promote his upcoming film The Slightest Touch, Farrell was asked about playing the Penguin once again.

“I'd love to. I'd love to do a second season. There's a conversation to be had,” he replied. Farrell then talked about his role in The Batman Part II.

“So the Batman film, they're doing the sequel to The Batman, and I did two scenes in that. Just that. In and out. It was a bit tasty to do it. I was kind of moaning about the makeup again, but I do love the character and I'm very protective of the character. And there's definitely a conversation to be had about doing a second season.”

The Batman movies are from writer and director Matt Reeves, who recently drafted in Ocean's 11 director Steven Soderbergh to help him finish principal photography on the sequel while he deals with a personal matter. Those Batman films, alongside The Penguin TV show, form part of what is called The Batman Epic Crime Saga, which is separate to James Gunn’s rebooted DC Universe.

Gunn’s plan was to introduce a Batman of his own with The Brave and the Bold, but after this week’s dramatic news about his and fellow DC Studios co-CEO Peter Safran's exit from the company, the future of the DCU and indeed a third potential Batman movie from Matt Reeves is up in the air. New Warner Bros. owner Skydance has yet to outline its plans for DC movies and TV shows, with both Gunn’s Man of Tomorrow and Reeves’ The Batman Part II still down for release in theaters.

As for Farrell, in June he said he had read The Batman Part II script, which was written by Reeves and Mattson Tomlin, and loved it. Speaking to ScreenRant, Farrell described the script, and his involvement in the movie.

items.title: Mass Effect Could Still Be Saved, Ex-BioWare Developer Suggests, With Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 Holding the Key
items.description: The future of Mass Effect could be secured with a key learning from the beloved Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, a former BioWare veteran has suggested.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
The future of Mass Effect could be secured with a key learning from the beloved Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, a former BioWare veteran has suggested.

In the days since EA announced it was shutting down its storied RPG game studio and killing its in-development Mass Effect Universe project, discussion has turned to the costs behind creating another AAA-budget entry in BioWare's space opera series, following a report that EA decided to invest in Star Wars instead.

Last week, BioWare co-founder Trent Oster suggested that EA would likely have been on the hook for at least $200 million in development costs to finish Mass Effect Universe at a level that fans expected.

"Rough ballpark (based on contemporaries) is $200m+," Oster wrote on X/Twitter. "That is a big number to commit up front. There has to be a bigger plan in place for the IP to make the math work." (To be fair, there is still that Mass Effect TV series in the works. And there certainly won't be any bigger plan in place for the IP if its flagship next game is cancelled.)

Now, Mass Effect lead programmer Christina Norman has said the game could be made for around $50 million — a figure that is five times the budget spent by the makers of Clair Obscur.

Highlighting a report on the French-made RPG's overall budget, which was pegged at less than $10 million, Norman wrote on X/Twitter that this was "a good example of why I think another Mass Effect game could be made for well under 200 million.

"I mean 5x the budget of Claire obscure expedition 33 should be more than enough," she continued. "You can always spend more but clever small teams can get it done."

Norman spent more than six years at BioWare working on the original Mass Effect trilogy, firstly as a lead programmer responsible for creating the franchise's conversation system, before moving on to become lead designer for Mass Effect 2 and 3, working to improve the series' gameplay.

In the years since, Norman served stints at Riot Games and her own co-founded startup, before becoming a full-time machine learning engineering consultant focused on LLM-directed character conversations. Still, there's no suggestion that LLM technology would be needed to turn in Mass Effect Universe on a smaller budget.

Even Oster has said he believed a new Mass Effect could be made for "cheaper" than $200m, though it "wouldn’t be what the team described in the Universe concept," he wrote in a follow-up post. Alas, Oster also highlighted another big blocker to a new Mass Effect being made — that EA still owns the franchise's rights, and may never want to give them up, even if it's not actively using them. "The big push would be getting the IP free," he concluded. "The fans deserve more."

Last week's annual N7 Day celebration of the Mass Effect franchise featured the Normandy's cast and crew teaming up for a video message asking fans to help save Mass Effect. This followed an array of footage and details for the canceled Mass Effect Universe appearing online, and a petition for EA to reconsider its decision which has gained more than 325,000 signatures. A Canadian politician also started a government petition to save BioWare just last week.

items.title: Avengers Endgame: Encore Finally Gets a Disney+ Release Date, And It's Real Soon
items.description: Avengers Endgame: Encore will get an imminent Disney+ launch, it's been confirmed.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Avengers Endgame: Encore will get an imminent Disney+ launch, it's been confirmed.

The updated and extended version of Avengers Endgame will premiere via Disney+ as soon as this week, on Friday, November 13. That's according to an official listing now visible to subscribers in the U.S.

While a Disney+ arrival for Endgame's re-release always seemed likely, Marvel had held off providing official confirmation — likely to drum up more FOMO for audiences to watch in theaters. Indeed, the company also kept exact details of how it had extended Endgame under wraps until the film's cinematic debut in September — at which point its new scenes promptly leaked online.

Of course, fans have been able to watch Avengers Endgame via Disney's streaming service for years. But the Encore version is technically new, with fresh color grading and a series of additional sequences shot during the production of this year's Avengers: Doomsday.

Encore's most notable change to the original film is its extended version of Endgame's final scene, which previously concluded with Steve Rogers and Peggy Carters getting an uninterrupted happy ending. In Encore, however, this finale is abruptly halted by the arrival of Loki — seemingly from his time working as a TVA agent.

Other new scenes follow in fresh mid-credits and post-credits additions. This includes a found footage-style scene featuring Bruce Banner, set after his appearance in Spider-Man: Brand New Day, and a scene set within the TVA featuring numerous characters from the Loki series.

Finally, the movie now concludes with the original hammering of metal — previously a callback to Tony Stark forging the Iron Man mask — revealed to be Doctor Doom forging his own appearance. It's a neat tease for any future similarities between the two characters played by Robert Downey Jr.

Of course, these elements have all been added to tease the upcoming Avengers: Doomsday — and position that film primarily as an Endgame sequel rather than what it also is: the beginning of the end for Marvel's divisive Multiverse Saga.

With Avengers: Doomsday now just over a month away, the time feels right for Avengers Endgame: Encore to hit Disney+. It'll also arrive just days after another huge Doomsday tease arrived on Disney+ this week via a shocking post-credits scene in the finale of Vision Quest (beware spoilers!)

items.title: Nintendo Defends Decision to Cut Mario and Yoshi Easter Eggs From The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake
items.description: Nintendo has defended its decision to scrub the secret appearance of Mario characters from its The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Nintendo has defended its decision to scrub the secret appearance of Mario characters from its The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake.

Hidden away inside Hyrule Castle, the game's original 1998 version included a wall of portraits that featured Mario, Luigi, Peach, Bowser, and Yoshi artwork taken from Super Mario 64.

Visit the same area in Nintendo's newly-launched Switch 2 version, however, and all references to the Mushroom Kingdom have been removed. On a similar note, a selection of Zelda: Twilight Princess artwork has also been cut, having been snuck in when Ocarina of Time was re-released on 3DS.

Now, Nintendo has addressed its choice to remove these Easter eggs — and said that what was once a more "carefree" approach within Nintendo to referencing other games has been reconsidered.

"Certainly, at the time, when we put those there, I don't think anybody thought it was too big a deal," legendary Zelda series producer Eiji Aonuma told Game Informer. "Maybe there was a more carefree or comfortable approach to that sort of thing.

"But looking at it now... given the overall way that we're creating this world and giving the player that form of expression, if they look up and they think, 'Why is Yoshi there?' We don't want that moment to interrupt their experience of the world in that way. So we're feeling a little bit differently about it this time."

While some fans might feel like it's a shame to see this more carefree attitude to Easter eggs is gone, it's fair to point out that Mario 64 Easter eggs (or Skyward Sword ones, for that matter) would make less sense today. Mario 64 was launched on the same platform as Ocarina of Time, of course, while Skyward Sword was released contemporaneously with the game's 3DS port. (Maybe Switch 2 just needs a new Mario game to actually arrive?)

"I do remember at the time the designers on the 3DS version were really interested in placing Easter Eggs like that throughout the game," Aonuma continued, "and the timing of the release of Skyward Sword was such that it was perfect to go ahead and include that... [But] you don't want to interrupt the player's experience by seeing something that's unrelated to what they're currently doing in the game. So for that reason, we decided not to go that way."

"No hard feelings there," commented Skyward Sword director Hidemaro Fujibayashi, who returned as a producer for this remake.

And one Mario reference does still survive via Talon — a character who is an obvious nod to Mario with his bushy moustache, plus red and blue overalls. Check out his necklace, and you'll see his golden Bowser charm remains intact, all these years later.

Nintendo legend Shigeru Miyamoto has previously discussed the idea of the company's different franchises crossing over, and said that he wasn't a fan — except when it is Pikmin, which he wants to include wherever possible.

Earlier today, Nintendo revealed that Ocarina of Time had already shifted 5.2 million copies and become the Switch 2's fastest-selling game so far. Meanwhile, players have been having fun in-game by performing everything from Linkin Park to the Titanic theme on ocarina.

items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
The much anticipated remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time launched on November 5, and one feature has fast become a big hit: the fact that you can now play any tune you like on Link’s ocarina. Now, social media has become awash with players sharing the results.

People are tackling tunes from other video game series like Final Fantasy, anime such as Dragon Ball Z, and film scores including Titanic and The Lord of the Rings. Users often put a pun in the post, usually involving Link or Hyrule.

Over on X, @StevenxTCG got Link to play Linkin Park’s ‘In the End’ on the ocarina. The post proved unexpectedly popular, prompting him to follow up with a guide on how to play it yourself. On a more upbeat note, another poster responded with ‘Macarena of Time,’ their take on the '90s dance craze.

Perhaps predicting this trend, Nintendo also released an official Playable Ocarina. This physical replica of Link’s musical instrument comes with the added bonus that it can also be used with the game. If you play a melody towards the Switch 2’s microphone, Link in the game will play along with you.

Of course, playing songs on Link’s ocarina is also a game mechanic. By finding and learning songs, Link can do all manner of useful things like fast travel and solve puzzles. Check out our guide if you are struggling to find any of the 13 in-game songs.
